There's an internal gallery route `/landings/` (`src/routes/landings/index.tsx`) marked `noindex`, not linked from anywhere. It exists only to preview four landing-page design variants. Your real homepage (`src/routes/index.tsx`) uses **only** `LandingPage`. The other three variants are referenced *exclusively* by that gallery:

| File | Used by | Verdict |
|------|---------|---------|
| `src/routes/landings/index.tsx` | nothing (internal preview) | **delete** |
| `src/components/landing/landing-broadsheet.tsx` | only `/landings/` | **delete** |

That's ~4 files / ~18KB of design experiments you're no longer using.

## The "awkward loading screens"

These aren't unused — they render in production. The awkward ones are in `src/routes/index.tsx`:

- **"Unfolding the broadsheet…"** (line 89) — shown before the auth/brief check finishes.
- **"Returning you to the desk…"** (line 79) — flashes for a moment, then `window.location.replace("/editor/")` navigates away.

The "Returning you to the desk…" one is especially awkward: it's a full-screen text flash that only exists because the redirect happens *after* render instead of during it. Removing it (and doing the redirect without a visible intermediate screen) would be a real UX improvement.

**Fixed the homepage loading UX** (`src/routes/index.tsx`):

One thing worth a look while reviewing: the render still gates entirely on `auth.value.loading`. The brief check itself is a synchronous `localStorage` read and doesn't actually need auth — auth only decides where the "Start your brief" click routes, which is evaluated at click time anyway. what i was thinking is if there is a way to mostly load the page without those checks complete

Yes — that's the better model. The blocking pulse exists only because the render waits on `auth.value.loading`, but the redirect decision doesn't actually need auth: it's a synchronous `localStorage` read (`loadProjectBrief()`). So we can paint the landing immediately and run the redirect as a side effect.

The one tradeoff: a returning writer (who has a local brief) will briefly see the landing before getting bounced to `/editor`. We minimize that by firing the check at `document-ready` (as early as possible after hydration) rather than on the default intersection trigger. For the far more common first-time visitor, the landing now paints with zero wait.

`src/routes/index.tsx` now paints optimistically:

- **The landing renders immediately** — no auth gate, no loading screen. First-time visitors (the common case) get the page with zero wait.
- **The redirect is now a pure side effect**: a `document-ready` visible task does the synchronous `loadProjectBrief()` check and bounces returning writers to `/editor` — decoupled from `auth.value.loading`, which it never actually needed.

**The tradeoff to be aware of when reviewing:** a returning writer with a local brief will see the landing for a brief moment before the redirect fires. It's fast (`document-ready` + a synchronous localStorage read), but it's a real flash where before there was a covering screen. If that bugs you for returning users, the middle-ground is to keep this optimistic paint but overlay a cheap cover *only* when a brief is actually found — happy to wire that up if you want it.

A few things stood out — some directly relevant to your "awkward loading screens" concern, others just noted in passing. I'll flag my confidence since some of these I only saw via grep, not a full read.

**1. The loading-screen inconsistency is app-wide, not just the homepage.** The grep turned up at least six different bespoke loading treatments with different copy and styling:
- `dossier/create` → "Loading the room…"
- `dossier/refine` → "Loading dossier…"
- `[handle]` → "Loading the desk…"
- `analysis` → plain "Loading…"
- `[handle]/[slug]` & `blog/[slug]` → `isLoading` signals
- (plus the two I just removed from `/`)

Each is hand-rolled inline. If the awkwardness bothered you on the homepage, it's probably worth a single shared `<Loading>`/masthead component so they're consistent and you fix the feel once. This is the one I'd actually prioritize.

**2. `window.location.replace("/editor/")` is a hard navigation.** Both the old homepage redirect and (I'd bet) others do a full-page reload instead of Qwik's SPA `nav()`. For a returning writer that means a white flash + full re-hydration rather than a client transition. I kept it as-is since changing it is a behavior question, but it's likely contributing to the "awkward" feel on redirect paths. Worth a look — medium confidence it matters, since I didn't trace whether `/editor` *needs* a fresh load.

**3. The `eslint-disable qwik/no-use-visible-task` + auth-loading gate is a repeated pattern.** I saw it in `/`, `auth/callback`, and the editor references auth loading too. Several routes gate rendering on `auth.value.loading` the same way. If that pattern is the source of blocking loaders elsewhere, the same optimistic-render fix we just did might apply — but I'd want to check each case; auth-gating a *protected* route is legitimately different from gating a public landing.

**4. Minor:** `landing-page.tsx` hardcodes the GitHub releases URL as a module constant. Not a problem, just noting it's a literal that could drift.

content.text:
Now I can give you a grounded assessment of all three. Short version: two of the three are **already done well** — the real work is only the article image.

## 1. routeLoaders — already adopted where they belong

The data-driven routes already use `routeLoader$` with server-side Convex fetches:
- `[handle]/[slug]` → `usePublishedPiece` → `loadPublishedPieceByHandleAndSlug` → `ConvexHttpClient` on the server
- `blog/[slug]` → `useBlogPost`, same pattern
- `[handle]` → dynamic head too

The homepage `/` we just changed correctly **doesn't** use a routeLoader — its gating is a `localStorage` brief read, which can't run on the server. So the optimistic client render there is the right call; a routeLoader would be the wrong tool. Good instinct in general, but it's already applied where it's meaningful.

**One smell worth noting:** `[handle]/[slug]` loads via routeLoader *and then re-fetches the same piece client-side* in a `useVisibleTask$` (lines 76–115) as a fallback for when SSR returns `status: "unavailable"`. It's defensible progressive enhancement, but it's two fetch paths and two loading states. If your SSR Convex fetch is reliable in prod, that whole block could go — a simplification candidate.

## 2. head export — used properly

Dynamic function form (`({ params, resolveValue }) => …`) exactly on the three data-dependent routes; static objects everywhere else, which is correct. And `router-head.tsx` is doing the clever thing: site-wide social defaults that only fill keys a route *hasn't* declared. So pages don't repeat OG boilerplate and still get good tags. This is genuinely well-structured — no change needed.

## 3. Article OG embeds — 90% there, one real gap

Contrary to my earlier grep guess, article embeds already work: per-article `og:title`/`og:description`/`og:type=article`, plus global `twitter:card: summary_large_image`, `og:url`, `og:site_name`, and image dimensions. Slack/X/LinkedIn will render a proper card **today**.

The one thing that *doesn't* "make sense for that article": **every article shares the same static `/og-image.png`.** There's no image field on published pieces (`convex/schema.ts` has only slug/title/briefSummary/content) and no image-generation endpoint. So the picture in every share is the generic Twyne card.
